f: Aria is an Indian singer and lyricist under BeBy Entertainment. She is the maknae of the girl group X:IN, and a former member of the project group Triple iz and the girl group MEP-C formed through the training platform Universe. In early 2022, Aria, under the name of Ami, joined GBK Entertainment and became a trainee under their online training platform Universe, which aims to select girls to become potential members of a future girl group. She was born in Thiruvananthapuram. Prior to pursuing a career in the Korean entertainment industry, she worked as a child actor in Malayalam cinema, appearing in films such as Melvilasom and Thank You. In 2022, she moved to South Korea to undergo formal idol training under GBK Entertainment's online platform, Universe before officially debuting as vocalist of the multinational K-pop girl group X:IN in April 2023 under Escrow Entertainment with their single "Keeping the Fire." Recognized as the second person from India and the first of Malayali ethnicity to enter the K-pop industry, Aria attracted widespread attention across Asian media and social media platforms for her multilingual fluency in English, Korean, Malayalam, and Hindi. In addition to her vocal and performance roles, she has actively contributed as a lyricist to several of X:IN's musical releases, including tracks on their projects The Real and Defend Myself. Through her work with X:IN and participating project groups, she continues to serve as a prominent figure representing Indian talent in mainstream South Korean pop music.

b: Dr. Shashi Tharoor is a former union minister and four time member of parliement representing Thiruvananthapuram constituency. He is a former diplomat, internationally acclaimed author, and public intellectual. He…
f: Dr. Shashi Tharoor is a former union minister and four time member of parliement representing Thiruvananthapuram constituency. He is a former diplomat, internationally acclaimed author, and public intellectual. He earned his doctorate in international relations from the Fletcher School of Law and Diplomacy at Tufts University at the remarkably young age of 22. He spent nearly three decades in the United Nations, rising to the position of Under-Secretary-General for Communications and Public Information under Secretary-General Kofi Annan. In 2006, he was nominated by the Government of India for the post of UN Secretary-General, finishing as the runner-up in the global selection process. After leaving the United Nations, Dr. Tharoor entered Indian politics as a member of the Indian National Congress and won a seat in the Lok Sabha in 2009. Over his political career, he has served in various key governmental and parliamentary roles, including Union Minister of State for External Affairs, Union Minister of State for Human Resource Development, and Chairman of the Parliamentary Standing Committee on External Affairs. Beyond his political duties, he is one of India's most prolific writers, having authored numerous bestselling fiction and non-fiction works, including The Great Indian Novel, Inglorious Empire: What the British Did to India, and Why I Am a Hindu. Widely recognized for his eloquence and formidable vocabulary, Dr. Tharoor remains a prominent commentator on global politics, Indian history, and foreign affairs.

b: Geetanjali Shree is an acclaimed Indian Hindi-language author and scholar celebrated for her distinct narrative style and significant contributions to contemporary literature. Born Geetanjali Pandey in Mainpuri, Uttar…
f: Geetanjali Shree is an acclaimed Indian Hindi-language author and scholar celebrated for her distinct narrative style and significant contributions to contemporary literature. Born Geetanjali Pandey in Mainpuri, Uttar Pradesh, she completed her education at Lady Shri Ram College and Jawaharlal Nehru University in New Delhi before completing her PhD on Munshi Premchand at Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda. She made her literary debut with the short story Bel Patra in 1987, followed by her first story collection, Anugoonj, in 1991. Over her career, she has authored five novels-including Mai, Hamara Shahar Us Barsa, Tirohti, Khali Jagah, and Ret Samadhi-alongside several short story collections and academic works. In 2022, the English translation of her novel Ret Samadhi, titled Tomb of Sand and translated by Daisy Rockwell, achieved global acclaim by winning the International Booker Prize. This historic milestone made it the first novel translated from Hindi, as well as the first by an Indian author, to receive the prestigious international award. Beyond her fiction writing, she is an active member of the creative group Vivadi, contributing to theatre, arts, and cultural initiatives. In recognition of her literary achievements, she has received numerous accolades, including the Indu Sharma Katha Samman and prestigious fellowships from the Ministry of Culture and the Japan Foundation, as well as being named to the BBC's 100 Women list in 2022.

b: Meg Mason is an acclaimed Australian author and journalist renowned for her witty, deeply empathetic observations on family life, marriage, and mental health. Born in New Zealand, she grew up in Palmerston North before…
f: Meg Mason is an acclaimed Australian author and journalist renowned for her witty, deeply empathetic observations on family life, marriage, and mental health. Born in New Zealand, she grew up in Palmerston North before moving to Australia, where she completed a Bachelor of Arts degree at the University of Sydney. She began her career as a journalist, working for prestigious publications including The Financial Times, The Times in London, and GQ, along with writing columns for Vogue Australia and Elle. She made her literary debut in 2012 with her memoir Say Mumma!, which explored the humor and challenges of early motherhood, followed by her first novel, You Be Mother, in 2017. Mason achieved international commercial and critical acclaim with her 2020 novel Sorrow and Bliss, which masterfully balances dark humor with a poignant portrayal of living with chronic mental illness. The novel became a global bestseller, was translated into over twenty languages, and won the Fiction Book of the Year at the 2021 Australian Book Industry Awards while being shortlisted for the prestigious Women's Prize for Fiction. Currently residing in Sydney with her husband and two daughters, Mason remains a prominent voice in contemporary commercial and literary fiction.

f: Saurav Das is an investigative journalist, transparency activist, and chief spokesperson for the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP). He specializes in utilizing the Right to Information (RTI) Act to access government records, hold public institutions accountable, and analyze complex administrative and judicial proceedings. His work, which spans field reporting, legal analysis, and policy research, has been published across major national media outlets including The Hindu, The Wire, and Article 14. Through his independent journalism and public communication, Das focuses on highlighting governance issues, constitutional rights, and state accountability while producing explainers and educational workshops aimed at empowering citizens and student movements.

b: Sonam Wangchuk is an acclaimed Indian engineer, educator, and environmental innovator from Ladakh, widely recognized for his transformative contributions to mountain ecology, sustainable architecture, and educational…
f: Sonam Wangchuk is an acclaimed Indian engineer, educator, and environmental innovator from Ladakh, widely recognized for his transformative contributions to mountain ecology, sustainable architecture, and educational reform. Born in Leh district in 1966, he graduated with a B.Tech. in Mechanical Engineering from the National Institute of Technology Srinagar and later specialized in earthen architecture in France. Wangchuk gained international prominence as the founding director of the Students' Educational and Cultural Movement of Ladakh (SECMOL), established in 1988 to reform the public school system in remote regions. Through initiatives such as "Operation New Hope," he pioneered hands-on, contextual learning methodologies tailored to the needs of Ladakhi youth. He also co-founded the Himalayan Institute of Alternatives Ladakh (HIAL), an institution dedicated to higher education, vocational skills, and sustainable development in cold desert ecosystems. As an innovator, Wangchuk is celebrated for inventing the "Ice Stupa" techniqueþcone-shaped artificial glaciers designed to store winter stream water for agricultural use during dry spring months. His work extends to passive solar-heated earthen buildings and eco-friendly infrastructure, including solar-powered tents designed for military deployment in high-altitude environments. For his pioneering work in grassroots innovation and educational reform, he was awarded the prestigious Ramon Magsaysay Award in 2018 alongside several global architectural and environmental honors. In recent years, Wangchuk has also emerged as a leading voice for environmental conservation and constitutional protections for the fragile Himalayan region.
